title: Velvet Revolution in Czechoslovakia
description:
The **Velvet Revolution** was a non-violent transition of power in Czechoslovakia from November 17 to December 29, 1989. The revolution ended 41 years of communist rule in the country.

Mass demonstrations were triggered by a brutal police crackdown on a student march in Prague. Within weeks, the communist government resigned, and opposition leader Václav Havel was elected president on December 29.

The name "Velvet Revolution" refers to the peaceful nature of the transition. The revolution was a key part of the broader collapse of communist governments across Central and Eastern Europe in 1989.
